name: Chicken Vesuvio
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Source lists 580 cal / 26g protein. Chicken and potatoes roast in one pan and the peas go in at the end - a complete dinner in a single vessel, no side needed, which is rare in this slice. Built on whole-chicken and russet-potatoes, two of the cheapest board ids. Confidence high. | HARVEST:
intro_html: Chicken Vesuvio is Chicago Italian, born in the old neighborhood restaurants and never quite famous outside of them. Chicken and potato wedges roast in the same pan with garlic, olive oil, oregano, and lemon until the potatoes go crisp at the corners, and a handful of peas goes in at the end for color. It is a whole dinner in one pan with no side dish required. Each serving lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein for about ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 7.5 lb (3360 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 7.5 lb: ~$13.11. Buy 8 lbs: $14.16.
Chicken Broth, 1.2 cartons: ~$1.50. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 32oz cartons.
Lemon Juice, 2.3 lemons worth: ~$0.42. Buy 1 (lasts several batches).
Pantry seasonings (dried oregano, salt, black pepper, italian seasoning): ~$0.79. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $23.92 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.71 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $27.81 across 14 servings, roughly $1.99 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $17.72 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $45.53. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a complete dinner in one pan. Chicken thighs and potatoes are two of the cheapest items on the grocery board, which is exactly why this number looks the way it does.
shop_smart: Potatoes in the five pound bag are the best deal in the produce section, and here they are half the meal rather than a side you have to make separately. One pan, no extra starch to buy.
Boneless thighs are the cheap cut and they stay juicy through a hot roast. Breast would need babysitting and would cost more for the privilege.
Frozen peas cost almost nothing and beat fresh in every way that matters here. They go in at the very end and just need to warm through.
Lemon juice from the bottle is fine for this. The lemon is a background note under the garlic and oregano, not the star, so there is no reason to pay for fresh.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 425F. Cut the potatoes into thick wedges and toss them with some of the olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Season the chicken thighs with salt, pepper, oregano, and italian seasoning, then brown them hard in the rest of the olive oil in a large oven safe pan. Set them aside.
Add the potato wedges to the same pan cut side down and let them take on color for 5 minutes without moving them. That crust is the whole point of vesuvio potatoes.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, then pour in the chicken broth and lemon juice and scrape the bottom of the pan.
Nestle the chicken back in among the potatoes, put the pan in the oven, and roast 30 to 35 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir the butter into the pan juices off the heat so the sauce goes glossy.
Scatter the frozen peas over the top and let the residual heat warm them through, about 3 minutes. Do not roast them or they turn gray and sad.
portion_html: Set the full pan on the scale, subtract the empty weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Get chicken, potatoes, and peas into every container, and spoon the garlicky pan juices over each one before you close the lid. Every portion comes in at {{cal}} calories.

recipeIngredient: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh, 7.5 lb (3360 g)
steps: Heat the oven to 425F and toss the potato wedges with olive oil and oregano.
Brown the seasoned chicken thighs in an oven safe pan and set aside.
Sear the potato wedges cut side down until crusted, then add garlic, broth, and lemon juice.
Nestle the chicken back in and roast 30 to 35 minutes.
Stir butter into the pan juices and scatter the peas over to warm through.
Weigh the pan and divide into 14 containers.
